body:
The parent issue with description is #2690 

Proposed level changes for requirement in chapter "V7 Security Logging and Error Handling"

Full list of requirements for the chapter is listed here: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x15-V7-Error-Logging.md

| # | Description | Level change |
| :---: | :--- | :---: |
| **7.1.1** | [MODIFIED, MERGED FROM 7.1.2] Verify that when logging sensitive data, the application considers the protection level of the data. For example, it may not be allowed to log certain data such as credentials or payment details. Other data such as session tokens may only be logged having been hashed or masked, either in full or partially. | 1 > 2 |
| **7.2.4** | [MODIFIED, MOVED FROM 11.1.7, MERGED FROM 8.1.4] Verify that the application can detect and log unusual activity, including business logic anomalies and abnormal or excessive request patterns, such as by IP, user, total per hour or day, based on documented limits. | 2 > 3 |
| **7.2.5** | [MODIFIED, MOVED FROM 8.3.5] Verify that accessing sensitive data is logged (without logging the sensitive data itself) if this is required by relevant data protection requirements. | 2 > 3 |
| **7.4.1** | [MODIFIED] Verify that a generic message is shown when an unexpected or security sensitive error occurs, which does not expose sensitive internal system data such as stack traces, queries, secret keys, and tokens. | 1 > 2 |
| **7.4.3** | Verify that a "last resort" error handler is defined which will catch all unhandled exceptions. | 2 > 3 |

comments.body: I'm not sure about 7.4.1 being L2. This might mean exposing "secret keys, and tokens" to the user. It *does* fit the "another precondition must be met in order to exploit" though.

> I'm not sure about 7.4.1 being L2. This might mean exposing "secret keys, and tokens" to the user. It _does_ fit the "another precondition must be met in order to exploit" though.

I agree. It's also something that is typically very easy for the developer to implement at the framework level. So I suggest leaving it at L1 as well.
At the moment, I would like to keep the line that it is an extra mitigation or impact decrease for the situation if the error happens. It is not a first layer of defense.

@tghosth - From the 2nd layer of defense point of view, it is a clear L2. Now the question is, should we "override" it from a priority point of view, because it is an easy win - small effort for relatively big impact? On the other hand, I don't like this line to be misused for other situations where we have "L1 vs L2" discussions.

> Now the question is, should we "override" it from a priority point of view, because it is an easy win - small effort for relatively big impact?

From a developer perspective, I don't see this as an easy win. Especially if you didn't do logging in a centralised and effective way to begin with. This is another situation I am dealing with right now and it can be a bit like whack a mole.

To me it is also a strong 2nd level issue as you need access to logs to pull out the information.
